issue.title: write_event_store rewrites every bead event stream file on every mutation
issue.description:
Discovered 2026-08-16 while root-causing the bead-store wedge that blocked epic launches (fixed in sase-core 2233171, sase 5184f5ab0).

crates/sase_core/src/bead/jsonl.rs:288-306 in the sibling sase-core repo re-serializes and rewrites EVERY stream file on every bead mutation, not just the streams whose events changed. The store currently holds 853 streams, so appending a single note to one bead rewrites all 853 files.

Two concrete consequences, both observed:

1. Blast radius. A single event that is not round-trip stable wedges the ENTIRE store rather than one bead. That is exactly what happened: one 'resolution: null' event in sase-mk.jsonl failed to round-trip, and because every mutation re-emitted that stream, the append-only integrity guard refused every commit, push, and rollback store-wide. Error: 'cannot publish non-append-only bead event stream sase-mk: worktree rewrote ancestor event 5'. Per-stream writes would have confined this to sase-mk.

2. Latency. The failed 'sase bead work' for the primary_workspace_ownership epic reported slow_launch_stage phase_creation elapsed_ms=200901.7 and dependency_creation elapsed_ms=170376.8 -- each stage rewriting all 851 files then.

Verified the writes are currently byte-identical: after the round-trip fix, mutating one bead in a full 853-stream scratch copy changed only that bead's stream plus issues.jsonl, so git sees no spurious diff today. The cost and the blast radius remain.

Scope: make write_event_store write only the streams whose events actually changed, keeping events/manifest.json consistent and without weakening the append-only guard. Cross-repo: the change belongs in ../sase-core.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-li — a different root cause (concurrent sync silently deleting an event) in the same event-stream write path; a per-stream write change should be checked against that failure mode too.

Implemented per-stream bead event-store writes in linked repo sase-core. Changes: crates/sase_core/src/bead/jsonl.rs now has write_event_store_changed(), validates all streams before writing, writes only selected streams, and skips byte-identical atomic writes including manifest.json; crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation.rs now wraps event streams in tracked_streams::TrackedEventStreams so every mutable stream handout records the stream id, loaded event stores start with no changed streams, and legacy JSONL imports mark all streams changed for the first save. Added tests for selective writer/manifest reload, byte-identical write skipping, one mutation touching one stream file, the sase-mk blast-radius regression, and legacy JSONL first-save migration. Verification: focused cargo tests passed for write_event_store_changed_writes_selected_streams_and_reloads, atomic_if_changed_skips_identical_bytes, one_mutation_touches_only_the_mutated_stream_file, sase_mk_blast_radius_regression_preserves_unrelated_stream_bytes, and legacy_jsonl_migration_first_save_writes_every_imported_stream; sase-core just check passed. Scratch-store evidence on a copy of SASE_SDD_BEADS_DIR after the fix: 898 streams before/after, append note to top-level bead sase-10 took 934.129 ms, exactly 1 stream mtime moved (sase-10.jsonl), no streams created/deleted, events/manifest.json mtime did not move, issues.jsonl did move as expected. I did not run a pre-change scratch baseline in this session; the old code path rewrote every stream by construction. In the sase repo, just install succeeded against the linked checkout, then just check failed at unrelated mypy errors for HistoryWordCompletionMetadata in _history_word_rows.py:17 and _prompt_input_bar_completion_panel_labels.py:30; corroborated that existing active-epic issue on sase-n8 rather than creating a task.
